summary: Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford from circa 1980 to 1983. He held posts at the University of Kerala and at the Université catholique de Louvain, where he was a professor circa 1993.
Robert Drummond was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh. He served as a surgeon for the East India Company.

Robert Duquenne was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He served as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, and Padmanabh S. Jaini, and under Kusan Sunim and Gerald James Larson. He was Distinguished Professor at UCLA (circa 1993–2022).

Robert E. Harrist, Jr. works in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Columbia University, where he is attested in 2009 and served as the Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History (attested 2026).

Robert E. Morrell specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and teacher William H. McCullough. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (attested in 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda is a scholar in Indology and other fields who studied at the University of Oklahoma and mentored under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983). In 2008, he held adjunct posts at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.
Robert E. W. Iggleden was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw U Thittila from circa 1947 to 1952. He served as Secretary of the Pali Text Society until 1976.

Robert Ernest Hume worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Yale University, the University of Göttingen, and Union Theological Seminary, where he subsequently served as Professor of History of Religions from 1914 to 1943.

Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied as a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–2000 and 2012–2014).
Robert Fazy was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetology scholar who received his Dr.jur. from the University of Geneva by 1899. In 1939, he founded the Swiss Asia Society.

Robert Florida is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later held an Emeritus Fellow post at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (circa 1989–2006) and Vanderbilt University (2010), and held a post at the University of Southern California (circa 2006–2010).

Robert Gardner studied at Harvard University (B.A. 1947), where he later served as Professor (1956–1997) and founded an entity in 1957. He also held posts at the Harvard Art Museums and the University of Puget Sound.

Robert Gauthiot was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Buddhist studies who studied under Antoine Meillet at the EPHE and the University of Paris. He taught at lycées and became directeur d’études adjoint at the EPHE in 1905.

Robert Gordon Latham, a scholar of linguistics, studied at Eton, King's College, Cambridge under Rasmus Rask, and the Royal College of Physicians. He held posts at UCL, Middlesex Hospital, and directed the ethnological department at The Crystal Palace (circa 1852–1863).

Robert Göbl was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and historical/archaeological studies. He studied at the University of Vienna (Ph.D. 1948–1950), where he later served as a Privatdozent in 1955 and as Director from 1965 to 1989.

Robert H. Brower was a Japanology scholar who earned degrees from Harvard and the University of Michigan. He held posts at the University of Minnesota, Stanford University, the IUC, and chaired Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Leonard C. D. C. Priestley. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at McMaster, Michigan, and UC Berkeley (appointed D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor circa 2003).

Robert Hamilton Blair Williams was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. and Ph.D. at SOAS University of London, studying under Ralph Lilley Turner. He served as Assistant Keeper at the India Office Records (1939–1946) and Lecturer at SOAS (1949–1953).
